definitions.gloss: to break in; to force one's way in; to burst in
definitions.explanation: Used for unauthorized entry, often with criminal or aggressive implications. Intransitive verb formed from 押す (to push) + 入る (to enter).

examples.english: A robber broke into the house.

examples.japanese: ⟦{不審者|ふしんしゃ}→不審者：11348_fushinsha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{押|お}し{入|い}り、⟦{現金|げんきん}→現金：02716_genkin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{奪|うば}った→奪う：01895_ubau⟧。
examples.english: A suspicious person broke into the store and stole cash.

examples.japanese: ⟦{警察|けいさつ}→警察：01393_keisatsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{容疑者|ようぎしゃ}→容疑者：15039_yougisha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{押|お}し{入|い}った。
examples.english: The police forced their way into the suspect's room.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: ⟦{自動詞|じどうし}→自動詞：10977_jidoushi⟧ (intransitive). No transitive pair. Formed from ⟦{押|お}す→押す：02854_osu⟧ (to push) + ⟦{入|い}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧ (to enter), so the entry is forced rather than merely unauthorized.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- [place]⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{押|お}し{入|い}る - to break into [place]. The place takes ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧, never ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧.
- ⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{押|お}し{入|い}る - to break into a house
- ⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{押|お}し{入|い}る - to break into a store
- ⟦{強盗|ごうとう}→強盗：02818_goutou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{押|お}し{入|い}る - a robber breaks in

REGISTER:
Almost entirely a crime-reporting word. It appears in news copy and police statements about robberies and forced entries; in everyday speech people say ⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧ or ⟦{侵入|しんにゅう}→侵入：11440_shinnyuu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ instead.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{押|お}し{込|こ}む→押し込む：04237_oshikomu⟧ - to force something into a space (transitive; also used of a break-in)
- ⟦{侵入|しんにゅう}→侵入：11440_shinnyuu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ - to intrude, trespass (formal; covers unauthorized entry without implying force)
